verses.pali: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṁ attānaṁ samanupassamānā samanupassanti, sabbete pañcupādānakkhandhe samanupassanti, etesaṁ vā aññataraṁ.
verses.english: “Mendicants, whatever ascetics and brahmins regard various kinds of things as self, all regard the five grasping aggregates, or one of them.

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto
verses.english: It’s when an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

verses.pali: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
verses.english: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
verses.english: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

verses.pali: Iti ayañceva samanupassanā ‘asmī’ti cassa avigataṁ hoti.
verses.english: So they’re not rid of this way of regarding things, and the conceit ‘I am’.

verses.pali: ‘Asmī’ti kho pana, bhikkhave, avigate pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ avakkanti hoti—
verses.english: As long as they’re not rid of the conceit ‘I am’, the five faculties are conceived—
the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.

verses.pali: Atthi, bhikkhave, mano, atthi dhammā, atthi avijjādhātu.
verses.english: The mind, ideas, and the element of ignorance are all present.

verses.pali: Avijjāsamphassajena, bhikkhave, vedayitena phuṭṭhassa assutavato puthujjanassa ‘asmī’tipissa hoti;
verses.english: Struck by feelings born of contact with ignorance, an unlearned ordinary person thinks ‘I am’,
‘I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’.
The five faculties stay right where they are.

verses.pali: Athettha sutavato ariyasāvakassa avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati.
verses.english: But a learned noble disciple gives up ignorance about them and gives rise to knowledge.
With the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge, they don’t think ‘I am’,
‘I will be neither percipient nor non-percipient’.”
